subject: Modifying the Plots of plotNuse() and plotRle()

messages.subject: Modifying the Plots of plotNuse() and plotRle()
parts:
Hi,

I seem to be unable to figure out whether this question has been addressed or not so I apologize if this has already been asked.  Basically I have a set of U133 arrays which I have processed through aroma.affymetrix and now I am just using the QualityAssessmentModel() function to look at NUSE and RLE plots.  In particular, I am using the plotNuse() and plotRle() functions.  I have some simple tasks that I want to do such as modifying the names of the samples on the x-axes, but I can't find any parameters or any documentation on how to do this.

I know that plotNuse() and plotRle() "invisibly" return all the data so I could grab it all and then plot it.  But this seems overcomplicated for such a simple task and also the two functions will still plot it even though it returns the data invisibly.  

Does anyone have any ideas on how to do this?

Thanks

>
> I know that plotNuse() and plotRle() "invisibly" return all the data so I
> could grab it all and then plot it. But this seems overcomplicated for such
> a simple task and also the two functions will still plot it even though it
> returns the data invisibly.
>

> Does anyone have any ideas on how to do this.

First, those labels are the names of the arrays/chip effects plotted, i.e.

ces <- getChipEffects(qa);
labels <- getNames(ces);

You can dynamically change the names by using a fullnames translator
function (cf. http://aroma-project.org/howtos/setFullNamesTranslator),
e.g.

fnt <- function(names, ...) {
# Example appending "-foo" to all names
names <- sprintf("%s-foo", names);
names;
}
setFullNamesTranslator(ces, fnt);


Another, more low-level approach is the following. Internally, those
functions calls bxp() and passes additional arguments to it (via
'...'). So another way is to do:

plotNuse(qa, show.names=FALSE);
stopifnot(length(myLabels) == nbrOfArrays(qa)); # Sanity check
axis(side=1, at=seq(along=myLabels), labels=myLabels, las=2);

/Henrik
